This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/mcp`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s).

**32** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json efa2533dd88a6c8304761253c9916f81699c3dc9`.

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (literal, 35 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json efa2533dd88a6c8304761253c9916f81699c3dc9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cc21d00b02cd26f621edc9006229455ef61ec47a` — the merge of head `0d6ed3fa391f41511ae28ca7bfd457742dd3c2ef` into base `efa2533dd88a6c8304761253c9916f81699c3dc9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cc21d00b02cd26f621edc9006229455ef61ec47a && git checkout cc21d00b02cd26f621edc9006229455ef61ec47a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin efa2533dd88a6c8304761253c9916f81699c3dc9 0d6ed3fa391f41511ae28ca7bfd457742dd3c2ef && git checkout -B drift-repro efa2533dd88a6c8304761253c9916f81699c3dc9 && git merge --no-ff 0d6ed3fa391f41511ae28ca7bfd457742dd3c2ef

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json efa2533dd88a6c8304761253c9916f81699c3dc9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs efa2533dd88a6c8304761253c9916f81699c3dc9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Review — ACCEPT (`domain:cli` dispatch seat, default judgment tier)

Head reviewed: **`0d6ed3fa391f41511ae28ca7bfd457742dd3c2ef`**, compared once against the PR object's `head.sha` — identical, and **every one of the 33 check runs carries that same `head_sha`**, so no reading below is a dead-tree read. Taken against GitHub and `origin/main`; ⛔ none from the report, including where the two agree.

### ① Derived judgments

- **PR shape.** Base `main`, first line `Closes #16913` — correct: the delivered change is the card's whole ask. Whole-body scan: the only keyword-plus-number pair anywhere is `Closes #16913`; `#3746`, `#4001` and `#4134` each sit with no verb beside them.
- **Scope, from the changed-file list.** 3 files: `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`, its new test, and the changeset. Nothing unrelated, no `content/docs/releases/`.
- **Governed-surface fork: does not apply.** File list re-read at this head — **0** hits across `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`.
- **Clause-② gate, both legs unhit.** Path leg: **0** files under `packages/spec/src/**`. Declaration leg: `no`. ⇒ no in-seat contract review is owed before enqueue. Machine predicate at this head: `check-clause2-carriers --pair 17529` ⇒ **exit 0** (captured to disk before any pipe), 「the clause-② declaration is readable in the fixed spelling and both carriers agree, and its diff carries no widening tell」 — with its own caveat kept: 「A tell is not a proof and its absence is not one either」.
- **`Clause-②: no` verified against the diff, all three flip conditions**, measured rather than accepted: the file's export set is the ten pre-existing names only (`strictToolInput`, `UNKNOWN_ARG_HISTORY`, `OBJECT_NAME_ALIASES`, `RECORD_ID_ALIASES` are module-private); `strictUnknownKeyError` is **already published** at `packages/spec/api-surface/shared.json:123` (positive control: 125 quoted entries; a fabricated symbol returns 0); and the alias maps reach only the error factory at `:447-451` while the parsed shape is `.strict()` at `:454` ⇒ ⛔ nothing aliased is ever parsed, coerced or run.
- **CI, both reads.** 33 check runs collapsed latest-per-name: **28 success, 5 skipped, 0 not-green**. `Lint & Repo Gates` = `success`, `TypeScript Type Check` = `success`, `Check Changeset` = `success`. `GET /commits/0d6ed3fa/status` = **`success`** (`Vercel`), ⛔ not pending. `mergeable_state: clean`.

### ② A correction of mine, and it is not a quibble

I wrote on the card that this PR body 「carries **no** `Clause-②:` line at all」. **That was over-claimed.** The body did carry the declaration — as `` ## `Clause-②: no` `` — and my matcher missed it because the line began with `##` and a backtick. "Absent" and "present but unparseable" are different defects with different fixes, and the dev's diagnosis is the accurate one.

⭐ Verified the mechanism at source rather than taking it second-hand — `scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs:593`:

```
const CLAUSE2_KEY_LINE = /^[ \t]*(?:>[ \t]*)?(?:[-*][ \t]+)?(?:\*\*)?`?Clause-②`?(?:\*\*)?[ \t]*:(.*)$/;
```

Two independent reasons it did not match: the permitted line-start decoration is a blockquote `>` and a `-`/`*` list marker — **`#` headings are not in the set** — and the optional backtick is expected to close **before** the colon (`` `Clause-②`: no ``), where the body wrapped key *and* value together. The file's own docblock calls this shape a **near miss** and says near misses 「are not declarations」. ⚠️ Worth carrying forward: a `Clause-②` line inside a heading, or with backticks around the whole key-and-value, is invisible to the gate and reports as a near-miss — ⛔ not as an absence, which is what I called it.

The dev proved the fix two-legged by importing the real `readClause2Line` rather than re-deriving the grammar — a control leg returning `{"kind":"near-miss","reason":"spelling"}` on the published body and a candidate leg returning `{"kind":"declared","value":"no"}` on the sent one. ⭐ That is the right instrument and the right shape of proof, and it is what my own #17533 says is missing for PR **bodies**' closing keywords.

### ③ Recorded, not blocking

- **The footer landed at exactly one block.** The dev stripped the platform-appended block before sending — ⛔ never re-sending a body that already carries one — and let the `PATCH` channel re-append; read back byte-identical in the core with the stored length exactly **58 bytes** longer, which is the figure `references/platform-readings.md:320` already records for that cell.
- `Contract-text:` is parsed by no gate (`git grep` over `scripts/` and `.github/workflows/` ⇒ zero) and stays a prose carrier. Correct, and worth knowing.
- The dev flags `mergeable_state: unknown` on a `draft` PR where `draft` is the normal answer, explicitly did **not** act on it, and passed it up rather than treating it as a signal. ⇒ right call; my read at ACCEPT time returns `clean`.

### ④ Sweep outputs — criterion: *every `registerTool` site in the HTTP registrar, plus the two sibling registrars*

All **11** tools had the same split and none refused; the denominator held exactly. `mcp-server-runtime.ts` and `stdio-data-bridge.ts` were checked and left alone, and the reason for the runtime one is measured, not judged: its twelfth registrar converts the author's own `AIToolDefinition.parameters` and never silently strips — an open author schema keeps the key, a closed one refuses — so closing it there would override an author's declaration, the opposite direction from this card. Three notes carried as noted-not-filed, each with a named carrier; the `packages/mcp`-has-no-ratchet observation is anchored in the PR's own sweep test, which is driven off `tools/list` rather than a hand-written list.

### Verdict

**PASS — ACCEPT.** Path surface clean, every check green at this head, commit status not pending, closing keyword safe, clause-② `no` verified on the delivered diff. Flipping ready and arming auto-merge; the queue is the only landing path and ⛔ this seat never merges outside it. `pm:dispatched` stays on #16913 until MERGED is verified by measurement on `origin/main` — ⛔ never from the merge event.
